again: Good timing. The kettle has been doing nothing all afternoon and it was starting to sulk.
By the window, there is always a bit of light in here.

rain: Rain on those big windows sounds like somebody tapping to be let in. Never is.

again: You again. Have you come to watch me not catch anything? It is very restful.
My rod has seen more of this kitchen than it has of the river, to be honest.
morning: Up before the tide, I was. The tide did not thank me.

again: Did you hear that one go by? I had the window open before the whistle.
Wheesht a minute, the wains have gone quiet, which means trouble or sleep, and I am not sure which.
I will find you a biscuit before they do.
evening: Teatime in this house is a contact sport. Stand back from the table.

again: The teapot is still warm, near enough, so sit down.
Cian is at his Irish again. I hear 'tá' coming out of the room like a sneeze.
Well, look who it is. Come in, come in, you are letting the draught out.
I love a bit of company after a quiet day. The kettle is on, it is always on.
Good man yourself! I was only saying you would be in.
Sit in, there is a fire and a story, and I will do the story for free.

gale: Listen to that wind. I have been in worse, but I was younger and a bit thick.

again: Back so soon? That is the spirit. Homework always gets done faster on a second visit.
I have a pile of copies to mark, so you have rescued me from a long evening.
Traa dy liooar, there is no rush, sit down and have a cup.
I was just about to put the kettle on, which is how I know you were coming.
Ah, the visitor. I was starting to think you had sailed off without a word.
I do my best stories after the second cup, and it is the second cup now.

gale: A wind like that and I still look at the harbour. Fifty years of habit, that.

again: The kettle is hot, lovely, so you have timed it well, as ever.
I have a fresh batch of something on the side. I will not say what, in case it burns.
morning: Early for you! I have been up since dawn, with the cat, who is no conversation.

again: Back for another look? The walls give a bit more each time. Look at the colours near the bottom.
Most visitors do the full circuit in five minutes. You are clearly a person of taste.
Back for a second look at the catalogue? Browsers always buy in the end. Eventually. Possibly.
Same rates as before, which is to say, ours.
The building has not moved, I checked. It is very reliable.
If you ask nicely, I will point out a third carved head you may have missed.
morning: The marble floor is coldest first thing. A good place to wake up.

again: The numbers have changed since you were last here. They always do. It is the whole business.
Nobody comes to the same building twice unless they are either curious or lost. Good.
If you want to understand Dublin, read a bit, then walk a bit, then read it again.
Oh, you again. Grand. I have the kettle on and absolutely no reason to study.
I am avoiding an essay and you are an excellent excuse.
evening: I do my best thinking at night. It is also when I do my best snacking.

again: Is that yourself? You would make a decent corner back with a bit of training.
I was out on the pitch earlier. It is amazing how a puck of the ball clears your head.
Marvellous. I have been talking to the bicycle, and the bicycle has opinions.
There is always more to say about this city. I could go all night. Please stop me.
Ah, you are back. Sit, sit. There is tea, and there is a plate of something, and I am not sorry.
I was only thinking someone should call round. You have saved me the phone call.

rain: Soft day outside, as we say. Soft meaning it will soak you to the bone, but gently.

again: Back already? Come in, come in, mind the stair. I have the oven on for the scones.
My wee grandson was asking about you. He wanted to know whether you had seen the Castle yet.

fog: Aye, it is haar out there. Stay in, the scones will keep you right.

again: Ah, you are back. I was telling the cat about the Old Town again. She has heard it, but she is polite.
These stairs are the best exercise I get. Do not tell my doctor I said that.
Oh, hello again! You are just in time. Mum is making enough food for a small festival.
My wee brother is still practising his juggling. I am keeping score on the breakages.
The kettle is on, dear, and I have nothing to say about the bridge.
I have the best view in the street, if you stand on the right chair.
Gran has been telling the same story again. I have the whole thing memorised.
Do not tell her I said that.
morning: Mornings in this house are loud, because Gran is up first and she wants everyone to know it.

again: Archie needs somebody else to look glaikit at. Sit yourself there.
Have a cup of tea. I have a story about the neighbours and it needs an audience.
Come in, come in, there is always a spare cup. Out here you take any visitor you can get.
The wind has been at the windows all day. I stopped listening years ago.

gale: That wind is nothing, you should hear it in July. Well, no, you should not. Have a scone.

again: Get warm, it is a long walk from anywhere round here.
Sit yourself down. I have the kettle on and the midgies off, so it is a good day.
The kettle is still warm, and so, I hope, are you.
I think the dentist is already suspicious of me. He asks what I have been eating.
morning: Early start for the canal boats today. I could hear them from my pillow.

again: Did you tell anyone where you were going? I will ask every time, you know.
The kettle is on. The weather up the Ben is never what the forecast said.

winter: Winter up there is serious. It looks lovely from here, and that is the trap.

again: The kettle is on, and the cluricaun is quiet, so it is a good day.
If any more of my shoes go missing I am going to start charging him rent.
You are back! Did you see any boats? I count them every day from the window.
I am going to be a skipper when I grow up. Dad says I will have to be taller first.

gale: There is a big wind out. All the hookers will be tied up tight. I am not allowed out, which is rude.

again: Sit in, the kettle is on. At my age a visitor is better than the radio.
I have had my share of good days on that water, and a few cold ones. The good ones were better.

gale: Not a day for going out. I can smell it in my knee before it ever reaches the harbour.

again: Sit in, love, mind the cat, she has no manners.
Did I tell you about the yoke I could not find? It was in my hand. It was the yoke I was holding.
Have you come to help me mark? I will pay in tea.
Today was a very long lesson on the difference between 'there' and 'their'.
evening: Evenings are for marking, and for pretending that I am not about to stop marking.

again: Wipe your feet, hen. I will not ask twice, but I will mention it.
I have the kettle on and a full tin of tablet, so you are in luck, hen.
Well, come in out of the drizzle. Not that it ever stops.
A thousand trips on that Subway and it has never once been on time. I love it.

rain: It is dreich out there, as per usual. Stay in, it is not going to improve.

again: Excuse the stooshie, the place is a state and I am not apologising.
Granda would have loved a visitor. He had a story for every single rivet.
The cooplets still have it in for my chips. I have lost a war of attrition.
I would give you one but there are none left. Do not look at me like that.
There is always a pot of tea going in this house, and usually something with it.
My brother has stopped saying he is fine. That is a worrying sign. He is better today.
Back for a blether? Good. I was just wondering who I would talk at today.
Sit in by the fire, hen. The kettle has only just boiled, so you have timed it perfectly.
morning: Morning, hen. I have been up since six. At my age sleep is mostly a rumour.

again: Sit, sit, my lover, I was only just saying the house was too quiet.
The cat has been sulking since breakfast. You will be an improvement.

winter: Winter and the Holy Thorn is in bud, they say. I have yet to see it do so on cue, mind.

again: That dog has taken a shine to you. It will wear off.
Busy day on the farm, but there is always time for a cup. That is the secret of farming. Cups.
morning: Up with the cows, I was. They do not care what day it is. Very restful, in a way.

again: Excuse the mess. It is not a mess, it is a system. A very messy system.
There is still mud in my boots from the clear-up, and that was weeks ago.
Back for a second look? The house reveals a bit more each time, mostly the smoke.
Stand by the hearth a minute. You will understand why they kept the peat fire going all day.

gale: That is a proper Hebridean wind. The thick walls and low roof were built for exactly this.

again: Oh, you are back. Good. I have done nothing since you left, and now I have company for it.
Mam keeps asking if the revision is going well. I keep saying 'it is going'.
evening: Evening and I am finally in the mood to study. This happens every single night, just before bed.
